R2-01.why: Strong, current sources (No Body No Problem! top-5 Oct Next Fest; Worst Class Ever #1). The crime-to-'hide it before Mom gets home' reframe is principle-level and matches the kid version suggested in the research. It sits in Roblox's proven 1vN hunter format (Flee the Facility, Granny-likes) with a meme-friendly theme that has no direct structural competitor (Clean the House! is PvE chores). One contextual button plus fixed-camera hotspots makes it fully mobile-safe. Costs: (1) NBNP's emergent physics hiding and its 'act normal' bluffing (voice-heavy on Steam) are replaced by a fixed hotspot table, so hiding is a menu choice rather than a clever improvisation, and replay value depends on content churn. (2) The Parent player has nothing to do for about 2:45 of a 5-minute round (PARTY plus PANIC), and that role carries the costume monetization.
R2-01.fix: Give the Parent an active pre-hunt phase, such as a phone-call or drive-home minigame that drops early-arrival 'surprise' clues, or random early returns. Add 2–3 free-placement 'improvised' spots per room, such as stacking items or putting them on the dog, so hiding keeps some physics creativity. Keep FREEZE as the no-voice stand-in for bluffing.

R2-02.why: Fart Together's one-thruster-per-player shared vehicle is ideal for no-voice play: coordination comes from watching the raft, each player needs one HOLD button, and there is no aiming. The research's crude 13M-visit copy shows it carries over to Roblox. The source is mid-tier, though (about 4k CCU demo, top-20 rather than top-5). The kinematic spline controller trades away some unpredictable physics comedy for netcode safety, which is the right call but makes it feel more scripted. Originality is moderate: this is close to a clone of the core, and Boat Together (about 8.2M visits) already owns 'row in sync'. The real points of difference are the vehicle roster and the context verbs.
R2-02.fix: Make the rotating vehicle gimmicks the headline identity (bathtub, shopping-cart rocket, sky balloon) and add a few genuinely physics-driven cosmetic wipeouts so failure stays funny. Ship Raft Race versus play early, because rafts bumping each other is what separates it from Boat Together.

R2-03.why: Worst Class Ever is the strongest current source on the list (#1 Oct Next Fest, about 300k demo players). The adaptation adds real ideas rather than copying the classroom: tagging only works inside the flashlight beam, the flashlight has a battery, and releasing the stick freezes you, which is an elegant, native mobile input. The source does not depend on voice. The risk is PC precision: spotting subtle movement in a crowd of 30 statues on a phone screen is hard for the Guard. The shimmer assist helps but may make the Guard too strong. The NPC-blend lane is crowded on Roblox (Be NPC or Die, DISGUISE, In Plain Sight, Prank the Teacher), and WCE launched Nov 9, so direct WCE clones will reach Roblox well before a 3–4-month build.
R2-03.fix: Lead marketing with the flashlight/battery and freeze-on-release hook, not 'blend in with NPCs'. Tune the Guard's assist on real phones against the 5-inch-screen case. Cut scope to ship before the WCE clone wave settles, for example one museum wing and fewer Guard gadgets at launch.

R2-04.why: Swapping YAPYAP's voice incantations for traced runes is a principled no-voice substitution and the fusion idea is good. But YAPYAP's fun comes from shouting, mic mishears and moving through a tower you are wrecking. Removing movement, camera and voice turns it into a stationary wave-defence game whose real ancestor is Nitrome's Magic Touch, not YAPYAP. Tower defence is saturated on Roblox and Draw Spells Magic Arena exists. Gesture drawing is excellent on touch, weaker with a mouse, and close to unplayable on console controllers, which is a Roblox cross-platform gap. The 1-second fusion window will mostly fire by accident among 4 players, which is fine but cuts its strategic value.
R2-04.fix: Bring back some physical chaos: short apprentice movement between balconies, spells that knock teammates' hats off, or a destructible tower. Provide a console fallback, such as a radial rune selector with stick flicks. Market the fusion discovery log, not the tower defence.

R2-05.why: Probably Stolen is a strong source (660k+ demo players, 98% positive), and inspect-and-spot-the-fake has no evidence of a Roblox competitor, so originality is real. But its fun is solo economic risk (rent, a bust that ends the run). Grafting it onto Among Us-style deduction loses that, and it adds the riskiest piece for this audience: social deduction without voice or chat, where too little information reaches the vote. Young players have to learn two systems at once (tool inspection plus forger deduction) in a 6-minute round. Visual tells will be memorized quickly.
R2-05.fix: Make the PvE 'Open Shop' appraisal loop the core (solo or co-op, with streaks and rare-item collection and adaptive NPC forgers) and make the hidden-forger mode a secondary weekend mode. Give the deduction mode richer automatic evidence, such as footprint trails and a camera timeline, so votes don't depend on chat.

R2-06.why: The sources (I'm on Observation Duty, Exit 8) are older and already heavily mined on Roblox, including a licensed Exit 8 co-op. This is the most crowded lane. The Watcher/Patroller information split is a sensible no-voice twist (BOMBANANA and Big Walk principle). But spotting anomalies needs fine visual perception, which suffers on small CCTV thumbnails on a phone. Patrollers mostly follow arrows (low agency), and one Watcher per group is a single point of fun.
R2-06.fix: Rotate the Watcher every 60–90 seconds so everyone gets the information role. Show bigger, more exaggerated anomalies on mobile. Give Patrollers anomalies only they can perceive (sound or touch) so information flows both ways, as in BOMBANANA's cyclic chain.

R2-07.why: Content Warning is a strong source (6M+ claims), but its comedy comes mostly from proximity voice: friends screaming and narrating in the footage. On Roblox, with no voice for young players, the replay shows silent avatars ragdolling plus fake comments, so the core joke does not survive. Several small Content Warning-likes and many ghost hunts already exist. The 10 Hz CFrame replay is technically sound but cannot stand in for the missing audio. The concept is also thin.
R2-07.fix: Replace voice with performed reactions: one-tap scream and flail emotes with exaggerated audio stingers that the replay captures, auto-subtitles of 'reaction cards', and ghosts that pull silly visual pranks. Otherwise fold the replay theatre into a stronger concept, such as GROUNDED's report card.

R2-08.why: R.E.P.O.'s value meter is a proven hook. Per-parcel handling rules (cake sags if you run, aquarium sloshes on turns) are a nice principle-level twist, and removing horror fits kids. But much of R.E.P.O.'s fun is free-physics mishaps, proximity voice and monster pressure. Scripting the carry and removing threat leaves a gentle delivery obby. Handling rules that punish running and sharp turns clash with Roblox's analog mobile thumbstick, which has poor fine control. Clone saturation: E.R.P.O.-likes and Carry the Glass Together already exist.
R2-08.fix: Add a light chaos antagonist (a toddler or dog chasing the parcel) and lean on comedic failure rather than precision. Map handling rules to discrete inputs, such as a 'tiptoe' toggle button, instead of thumbstick finesse.

R2-09.why: Two top-tier sources: Mewgenics (115k CCU) for inheritance and mutation, and Merge Tactics (a mobile-proven Clash Royale mode with record revenue). Adding a breeding meta to an auto-battler is a principle-level combination, not a clone. It fits Roblox's pet and collection culture, and drag/tap with one timed tap is fully mobile-native. Neither source needs voice. Concerns: no avatar movement weakens Roblox's social and cosmetic presence. 150 mutations that change attack patterns is a heavy balance load for 2–5 developers (the Squad Busters warning about depth versus churn). 'Breed' framing should be softened for kids, as the research advises.
R2-09.fix: Add a walkable hub or nest where avatars and critters are visible, and play matches in a physical arena that avatars watch from. Start with about 40 mutations that change visuals plus one stat axis. Rename breeding to 'nest pairing' or a family tree.

R2-10.why: BOMBANANA is an excellent source (675k+ demo players, 1M wishlists, #1 June Next Fest), and the research rates its no-voice translation as a good fit with no Roblox analogue. But the redesign drops BOMBANANA's distinctive cyclic 3-role chain for a 2-player Keep Talking setup. Making the stamps identical to the manual symbols risks making relay trivial ('see symbol, tap symbol'), which removes the translation gap where the fun lives. Keep Talking's tension comes from frantic verbal description, and taps are slower and calmer. Pairing with strangers is the main mode. Puzzle memorization threatens 28-day retention.
R2-10.fix: Make the 3-role cyclic chain the main mode, with bot-filled roles, as in the source. Keep a translation step: the manual maps symbol → colour → position while the stamp wheel shows only shapes, so relaying takes interpretation. Use procedural rule seeds per session, not per season.

R2-11.why: Overcooked-style station co-op is a verified gap on Roblox, and putting it on a crashing vehicle is a decent principle-level move. Big flashing icons make it largely voice-free. But this is close to a known template (Overcooked or Lovers in a Dangerous Spacetime). IRON NEST, the newer and more interesting source, contributes almost nothing: its diegetic multi-step control panels are missing. The pilot drag-yoke role is the one precision-sensitive role, and Land or Die! and Survive the Plane Crash crowd the theme. The concept is underspecified.
R2-11.fix: Import IRON NEST's diegetic procedures: stations need 2–3 step lever sequences, with the 'how' shown as icons on another station, which creates no-voice interdependence. Make the pilot a corridor-snap lane choice, not free steering.

R2-12.why: It fits Roblox very well (firefighters plus pets plus a visitable sanctuary). Auto-aim spray and a contextual RESCUE button are mobile-safe with no voice dependence. But from a Steam-indie lens the grounding is weak: Flash Point is a board game, Pet Simulator is Roblox-native, and Overcooked and PowerWash are older. No 2026 Steam mechanic is being translated, so the 'indie edge' is limited, and auto-aim spray removes PowerWash's tactile satisfaction. Firefighter roleplay competition exists, but procedural co-op rescue plus collection looks open (unverified).
R2-12.fix: Restore one satisfying tactile verb on touch: a drag-to-sweep hose that visibly clears soot or flames, as in PowerWash. Borrow a current indie hook, such as R.E.P.O.-style fragile carry (critters panic if jostled) or Dumpster Gang-style downed-teammate rescue, to sharpen the moment-to-moment play.

overall_notes: Strongest adaptations take a current, proven Steam hit and translate its principle into a no-voice, one-button form: R2-01 (NBNP to 'hide it before Mom'), R2-03 (WCE plus flashlight-battery and freeze-on-release), R2-02 (shared-thruster raft) and R2-09 (Mewgenics plus Merge Tactics). None reaches 8: each either loses part of the source's emergent physics comedy to netcode-safe scripting or faces a crowded or fast-cloning Roblox lane. Weakest are those whose source fun depends on voice (R2-07 Content Warning, partly R2-04 YAPYAP and R2-05 deduction) or on perceptual precision in an oversaturated genre (R2-06 anomaly). R2-10 dropped the most distinctive part of its excellent source (the cyclic 3-role chain). Speed to market matters for WCE-, BOMBANANA- and NBNP-derived concepts because Roblox clones of Steam hits arrive within weeks (Meccha Chameleon precedent). Console-controller input is unaddressed for gesture concepts.
